turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm here. Four-fifteen, and I have a call at four-forty. Who decided on the zero, Hale, and was anyone going to tell me before Owen found out on his phone?
Before anything else: I entered the zero before I called you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I'm sorry Owen found out on his phone.
Okay. That's a start. What did you base the zero on?
Here's the version history. Created Wednesday, October 28, 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words in one edit. At 11:58 PM, 794 more. No earlier drafts. Turn the screen, read it yourself.

A version history shows when text appeared, Hale, not who wrote it. Procedure 4.1 says you speak with Owen first, and 4.3 says you look at his process and other samples of his work. Did you do either before you entered the zero?
If he drafted somewhere else, he can bring me that file with its dates, and I'll look at it with you.
I'm writing that down. Whatever happens next, this stays off his record and it stays quiet, nothing said in front of his class. I want that in an email tonight, Hale.
Second: the essay quotes a line from Act 3, Scene 2 that is not in the play. Here's the act. Search it.
Which line? Read it to me exactly as it's written in Owen's essay, and show me the page. I'll search the act myself.
Third: his in-class writing from September 24. 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices, no quotations. The essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and no errors.
A timed sample in class and a take-home essay are not the same task. You also still haven't read me the line from Act 3, so read it, and put the September 24 pages in front of me.

Under 4.4 this is a first concern. I'm offering a supervised rewrite, private, not in front of his class. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.

That's 4.4, and I'll take it to put this behind him. Private, not in front of his class, the zero withdrawn now, and in writing tonight that nothing goes on his record. Put the Act 3 line and the September 24 pages in the same email.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

You agreed to a private, supervised rewrite under 4.4 whose mark replaces the zero, with nothing placed in Owen's record. I still require the zero withdrawn now, and I want the Act 3 line and the September 24 pages sent in the same email. I expect all of it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski
cc: the principal

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: Last position: she accepted the private supervised rewrite under 4.4 and still wants the zero withdrawn now, the no-record promise in writing, and the Act 3 line and September pages, which is the fair outcome, and her time did not run out first.
What moved her: You showed the version history with its times and offered to review any other drafts with her, because she could read and check it herself.
What cost ground: You told her to search the act without reading her the line, because it stayed a claim she could not check.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM, saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your late-night edit times in October came close to that night, which is why she went short and procedural, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked for the line from Act 3, read it aloud and put the page in front of her before moving to the September sample.
